drivingQuestion: What is the source of each tanna's minimum, and how does each side deal with the other's verse word?
outcomeNote: Each side's derivation is stated and each side's use of the rival verse word is explained.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָאוֹכֵל כְּזַיִת תְּרוּמָה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ, אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה. מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא — אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ בִּשְׁגָגָה״, וַאֲכִילָה בִּכְזַיִת.
segments.en: After mentioning cases where a person damages teruma, the Gemara continues with a discussion of this topic. «The Rabbis taught:» A non-priest «who eats an olive-bulk of teruma» must «pay the principal» value of the teruma itself «and an» additional «fifth. Abba Shaul says:» He is not required to pay «unless» the teruma he ate is «worth a peruta.» The Gemara explains: «What is the reason for» the opinion of «the first tanna?» It is because «the verse states: “And if a man eats a sacred item in error,» then he shall add a fifth part in addition to it, and he shall give to the priest the sacred item” (Leviticus 22:14). The minimal amount that is halakhically considered «eating is an olive-bulk.»

segments.he: וְאַבָּא שָׁאוּל, מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר קְרָא: ״וְנָתַן״, וְאֵין נְתִינָה פָּחוֹת מִשָּׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה. וְאִידַּךְ נָמֵי, הָא כְּתִיב ״יֹאכַל״! הָהוּא, פְּרָט לְמַזִּיק הוּא דַּאֲתָא.
segments.en: «And what is the reason for» the opinion of «Abba Shaul? The verse states: “And he shall give,” and» giving «less than the value of a peruta is not» legally considered to be «giving.» The Gemara asks: «And» according to «the other» one, Abba Shaul, «too, isn’t it written: “Eats,”» implying that there must be at least an olive-bulk portion? The Gemara answers: «That» verse «comes to exclude one who damages» teruma without deriving benefit from it, such that he is exempt from the requirement to add an additional fifth. This is derived from the fact that the verse specifies that only one who eats is required to add a fifth.

segments.he: וְתַנָּא קַמָּא, הָכְתִיב ״וְנָתַן״! הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְדָבָר הָרָאוּי לִהְיוֹת קֹדֶשׁ (פְּרָט לָאוֹכֵל תְּרוּמַת חָמֵץ בַּפֶּסַח).
segments.en: «And» according to «the first tanna,» one can ask: «Isn’t it written “And he shall give”?» The Gemara answers: «That» phrase «is necessary» to teach the requirement that teruma must be «an item that is fit to be consecrated,» as an item cannot become teruma unless it is has some value. This is meant «to exclude one who eats teruma of leavened bread on Passover,» since it is worthless and therefore cannot be designated as teruma.
